Hi Alex / Priya — looping in technical details below. Quick overview first, then examples you can paste into your config.

High-level: what Redwood logs and options
- we capture request metadata (timestamp, route, model, token counts), request payload and response payload by default for diagnostics, and common HTTP headers. Trace IDs are captured but treated as potentially sensitive and can be transformed.

Storage & encryption
- Logs are stored encrypted at rest in our object store (customer namespace). You can select region (us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1) at provisioning time; logs are kept in that region by default.
- Retention: default 90 days (configurable per environment). We support 30/90/365 day presets or a custom window.

Redaction & masking options
- 1) Runtime redaction (recommended): we apply redaction rules at the API edge before persistence. Rules are applied to both headers and payloads.
- 2) Post-ingest processing: additional rules can run as a batch job to scrub older logs.

Examples (copyable)
- Mask emails: regex: "[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}" -> replace with "[REDACTED_EMAIL]"
- Mask account numbers (last-4 visible): regex: "\b(\d{6,12})(\d{4})\b" -> replace with "[REDACTED_ACC]****$2"
- Mask JWTs in Authorization header: header name: Authorization -> header value: mask token except token type (e.g., Bearer [REDACTED_TOKEN])
- Trace IDs: option A (default): keep trace IDs but hash them server-side before logging (sha256 -> store first 8 chars). Option B: drop trace IDs entirely.

Configuration snippet (edge config):
- logging: 
  - enabled: true
  - retention_days: 90
  - redaction: 
    - type: regex
      field: headers
      header_names: [Authorization, Cookie, X-Request-ID]
      pattern: "(Bearer\s+)?[A-Za-z0-9-_.]+"
      replace: "[REDACTED_TOKEN]"
    - type: regex
      field: body
      pattern: "[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}"
      replace: "[REDACTED_EMAIL]"

Operational controls
- you can:
- disable request/response body persistence entirely per environment (logs only include metadata).
- enable hashed trace IDs (non-reversible) for correlation without exposing raw IDs.
- whitelist IPs/roles that can access raw logs; access is audited and gated by KMS policies.

SOC2 / evidence
- attaching the SOC2 summary and a short checklist for auditors (see attachments). We also provide sample redaction rules in redaction-rules-examples.txt.

If you want, I can prepare a short demo of the edge config UI and how redaction applies in real-time.

From: Priya Shah <priya@fintechco.com>

Subject: Re: Thanks — logging controls & PII redaction follow-up

Thanks Dev — that is exactly what we needed. A couple of clarifying Qs before we schedule the tech session:

1) For hashed trace IDs: is the hashing done with a per-tenant salt (preferred) or global salt? We’d prefer non-reversible, tenant-specific hashing.
2) For the account-number masking example: can we enforce a policy that only the last 4 digits remain visible across all services? If so, we’ll want that as a requirement.
3) For retention: will setting 30 days impact our ability to triage incidents? What’s Redwood’s recommended best practice?

We’re >90% likely to move forward if the tenant-salted hashed-trace-id and enforced last-4 policy are supported. If you can confirm those two points in a short reply and share a calendar for the demo next week (we prefer Tue/Wed morning PST), we’ll lock in a time.

Thanks — Priya
Head of Platform Security, FintechCo
priya@fintechco.com
